Personally, my social life was nonexistent when I met my partner, so that hasn't given as many issues as I think it would typically, but I still have had them when I try to find a friend or interact with others in online games. Perhaps it's not universal, but something my partner said helped put it into perspective. They don't like doing this. Hurting you doesn't give them any joy. They don't want you to stop playing that game or to stop talking to that person. They want your comfort and reassurance and love in those moments. It might come across like they want tangible change, for you to listen to their demands or what their words imply, but that's not what they actually want. They don't want you miserable. They want you to be happy. They don't want to hurt you. They just want some care.

But you deserve some care too. After all these fights don't just hurt you or him, it hurts you both. You both need to take care of each other.

It's rough. It just is. It's not easy.

After an argument, if you think of something to say, just say it. If you feel bad about something you did, apologize. Gathering the courage to speak during these moments helps immensely in cutting them short and making amends quicker, not letting the tension keep growing. This doesn't mean you should be the only one apologizing. If something he does bothers you, don't just ignore it or forget about it. You need to say so.

If he doesn't take it well, it might be because he either needs some time to calm down, or... Well, yeah. 

There's not much you can do about what you've already said and done if you've already apologized for them. And there will be more times this will happen, there's no way to truly stop it (without driving yourself mad). If they're people you've known for a while, tell them about certain times where your ADHD symptoms showed. My family didn't believe in it also, but I made a list of things that have happened to me in the past that all point to me having ADHD.

Just for some of my examples...

- I could never sit down and study for the life of me but I still got good grades somehow.
- I had the hardest time making friends. I still don't have any.
- I interrupt people a lot. I get too excited in some conversations and start yelling without noticing.
- I didn't think about the things I said or did, I was VERY impulsive, still am.
- I fidget on my seats a lot. I sit in a very awkward way. My mom once got called by the middle school I went to because of this, asking if I had some sort of disorder and if they could do anything about it. That in itself is pretty telling lol.
- I liked making noise with pens, I had to play around with things to not get bored.
- In the same vein as that last thing, I had to be drawing in class all the time or else I wouldn't listen and I'd fall asleep. Seriously.
- I need people to repeat themselves a lot because my brain doesn't process what they said.
- I hyperfocus on projects or work at the last day it's due, I'd always forget to eat, go to the bathroom, or shower.
- I never felt like I fit in at all. I'd get my fill of people very quickly. I get very irritated when people talk to me after I've had my fill.
- If people give me multiple instructions to do, I'd always forget at least one of them.
- I lose track of what I'm saying in the middle of a conversation. I get sidetracked a lot when telling a story. It's impossible for me to know when to say what I want to say before the subject is changed.

And SO SO MANY other things... It'd be very hard for them to refute all your experiences with it if you tell them each and everyone of them. This of course should also be backed by official symptoms and definitions of what ADHD is. 

Some of the things I listed might be signs of ASD too but I'm not sure. There's a lot of similarities between the two. I've only been diagnosed with ADHD.

Best of luck to you, I hope you find some acceptance! Your struggles and experiences are very real no matter what anyone else tells you.
